objective: Localize the first reproducible PyTorch-to-frozen-ONNX activation divergence on the four frozen synthetic PE fixtures, determine whether discrete routing changes amplify kernel-level drift, and select a canonical native runtime path without opening any dataset, split, cache, prediction, or quality evidence.
scientific_questions: Does the known PE32 failure and PE32+ pass reproduce under an independently instrumented ORT_DISABLE_ALL session?
Which semantic activation boundary first exceeds the frozen 1e-6 absolute tolerance?
Do any TopK routing indices diverge before the final byte representation diverges?
Is the frozen ONNX lineage sufficiently specified and numerically stable to remain the preferred deployment representation?

probe_plan.phase_1: Compare byte encoder, PE projector, stat projector, fusion, classifier, logits, and every per-chunk input-projection/QKV/out-projection module boundary.
probe_plan.phase_2: Compare every exported TopK value and index tensor, retaining exact index mismatch evidence and float32 ULP summaries.
probe_plan.mapping_basis: Frozen ONNX node metadata namespaces plus deterministic PyTorch module hooks and torch.topk call order.
